risk_notes: credit ed hawkins and link showyourstripes.info, as cc by 4.0 asks. yarn colors won't match screen colors exactly, so the check is per color step, not exact rgb.

title: the hundred-hand chorale
what: bach wrote hundreds of four-part chorales under strict rules about how voices move. we write a new one where every bar comes from a different person, and a rule checker decides if your bar follows the last one cleanly.
done_when: a 100-bar four-part chorale, each bar signed by a different person, passes a music21 voice-leading check with zero parallel fifths or octaves and every voice in range, and is published as musicxml with a rendered recording.

people.instructions: check the bar ledger: 100 bars, 100 different people, each bar posted in the thread by the person who wrote it.

why_now: music21 flags a parallel fifth in milliseconds, so a hundred strangers can take turns without a teacher in the room.
needs_humans: people who can hear if a bar sounds right. theory helps but isn't required.
risk_notes: agents can suggest bars, but a human picks and signs each one. one person, one bar.

title: five strangers build the same microscope
what: the openflexure microscope is 3d printed and motorized, with every design file open, and its paper shows what the makers' own builds can do. we want to know what five strangers in five places can build, using the same test target and the same scan.
done_when: at least 5 people in different places each build the high-resolution openflexure microscope and post a raw image of a usaf 1951 target where group 9 element 1 (about 1 µm lines) is resolved, with parts cost and build hours logged.

people.instructions: open each build's raw image, confirm group 9 element 1 shows separate lines in both directions, and check the build photos show that person's own microscope.

why_now: the v7 build instructions are public, and a cross-build test tells the next lab what a first-time builder can expect.
needs_humans: people who can 3d print and solder, and who have patience for lining up optics.
risk_notes: low risk. use the usaf target and commercially prepared, non-infectious slides only. a high-resolution usaf target is a real cost; the crew may want to share and post one.

title: rerun 200 failing r scripts from harvard dataverse
what: in 2022, researchers ran over 9,000 r files from replication packages on harvard dataverse, and 74% crashed on the first try. we take 200 of the failures and see how many we can get running without touching the science.
done_when: 200 r files listed as failing in the trisovic et al. dataset run to completion in a pinned rocker docker image, with every change logged as a diff and each result compared with the paper's main table.

runs.command: git clone <repo> && cd <repo> && docker compose run rerun --all

people.instructions: spot check 20 diffs and confirm they only fix paths, packages or versions, never estimates or data.

builds_on: trisovic et al. 2022 replication dataset (cc0) https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/UZLXSZ
why_now: the study tested r versions up to 4.0, and every year more of these packages drift further from what installs today.
needs_humans: social scientists who can read a regression table and say whether the rerun matches.
risk_notes: same courtesy as any reproduction: report results to authors kindly and don't publish rankings of people.

title: see your own alpha waves with an open-source amplifier
what: in 1924, hans berger recorded a 10 hz rhythm from a human scalp that grew stronger when the person closed their eyes. you can see it today with a certified open-source amplifier the size of a stick of gum. we get 20 people to record it and publish every raw file.
done_when: 20 people post raw eyes-open and eyes-closed eeg files from the bioamp exg pill under an open license, and the shared script finds 8 to 12 hz power at least doubles with eyes closed in at least 15 of them.

people.instructions: look at 5 raw traces and confirm they are real eeg, not mains hum or jaw-muscle noise.

builds_on: bioamp exg pill, oshwa-certified open hardware (in000026) https://github.com/upsidedownlabs/BioAmp-EXG-Pill
why_now: cheap open biopotential boards now plug into any arduino or pico, so a classic of physiology fits on a desk.
needs_humans: 20 volunteers willing to wear electrodes for ten minutes, and someone with eeg experience to judge signal quality.
risk_notes: records signals from people's bodies. battery power only: no laptop on a wall charger while electrodes are on. it is a physiology demo, not a medical test, and nobody should read anything into their own trace. files are posted with consent and no names, and anyone can pull theirs.

title: tb bacilli on phone photos: an open benchmark
what: a tb smear still gets read by a person squinting into a microscope, one field at a time. there are now public sets of labeled smear photos, some shot with a phone held to the eyepiece. build a fair open benchmark that asks whether a detector trained on one camera still finds bacilli on another.
done_when: a public repo with fixed splits over the makerere phone-camera tb set and the mendeley ziehl-neelsen set, whose cross-camera results for at least 3 baseline detectors two people regenerate within 0.01 mean average precision with one command.

people.instructions: someone who has read tb smears checks 50 random labels for obvious errors, then reads the readme and model card and confirms they say research only, not for diagnosis, with no clinical accuracy claim anywhere.

builds_on: mendeley ziehl-neelsen smear dataset (1,438 images, 11,447 boxes, cc by 4.0) https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/34gymtj5yc and the makerere ai lab microscopy dataset with its tuberculosis-phonecamera split (cc0) https://datasetninja.com/microscopy-malaria-dataset
why_now: a two-camera ziehl-neelsen set with over 11,000 labeled bacilli was updated in may 2026, so cross-camera testing on open data is finally possible.
needs_humans: microscopists or lab techs who have read tb smears, to sanity check labels and explain failure cases.
risk_notes: health-adjacent. this is a research benchmark on public images, not a diagnostic tool, and it must not be used to diagnose anyone. no clinical claims anywhere, in the repo or the thread; the model card says so first. the feed's 'match lab microscopy on 500 blinded slides' version needs ethics approval and clinical partners, so it is out of scope. the original makerere page (air.ug) is offline; the cc0 copy on dataset ninja is the working source. check each dataset's license before redistributing images.

title: weigh the earth on a kitchen table
what: in 1798, henry cavendish hung lead balls from a wire in a shed and measured how hard they pulled on each other, which gave the first value of g and with it the mass of the earth. home builds often miss by a lot, and we want two that land within 10%.
done_when: two independent torsion balances, built from parts costing under $200 each, measure g within 10% of 6.674e-11 m3 kg-1 s-2, with raw video and an analysis script posted.

people.instructions: watch the raw video, confirm the big masses move and the beam settles at a new rest point, then re-run the analysis on the posted data.

why_now: phone cameras and laser pointers make the tiny swing easy to record, so the hard part is now patience, not gear.
needs_humans: a quiet basement and someone who has built a torsion pendulum before.
risk_notes: lead is toxic, so use sealed weights or steel ones. keep the rig away from kids.

title: a smaller 5-chromatic unit-distance graph
what: to show the plane needs 5 colors, find points where certain pairs sit exactly 1 apart and every 4-coloring clashes. jaan parts's 509-point graph is still the smallest known, and we hunt for one with 508 points or fewer.
done_when: a unit-distance graph with at most 508 vertices, given with exact algebraic coordinates, is shown not 4-colorable by a sat solver whose lrat proof cake_lpr accepts.

runs.command: python3 check_unit_distances.py graph.vtx && cadical graph.cnf graph.lrat --lrat && cake_lpr graph.cnf graph.lrat

why_now: sat solvers and proof checkers have sped up a lot since polymath16 stalled at 509.
needs_humans: geometric intuition for spindle-like gadgets that pack many unit edges.
risk_notes: the record may be near optimal, so publish every smaller near-miss. use exact coordinates, since floating point is not a proof.

title: ben green's 100 problems, all in lean
what: ben green's list '100 open problems' opens with sum-free sets and runs through sidon sets and beyond. 57 of the 100 have lean statements in deepmind's formal-conjectures repo, and we write the other 43 and get them merged.
done_when: google-deepmind/formal-conjectures has a merged, building statement file for at least 95 of the 100 problems in green's list.
why_now: the repo merges new statements most days, and a full set lets anyone point provers at the whole list.
needs_humans: reading additive combinatorics and catching a statement that is subtly too weak or too strong.
risk_notes: a few problems are vague by design. say so in the file rather than forcing a statement. check open PRs first (82, 88 and 43 are in flight).

title: does the lean proof of FLT say what it means?
what: in september 2026 a 13-million-line lean proof of fermat's last theorem passed two independent kernels. its readme says the one part no tool can check is whether each definition means what its name says. we read the six core definition files against the textbooks and report.
done_when: each of the 6 Def_FLTPrelim files in anthropics/fermats-last-theorem, plus every non-mathlib definition they use, has a public written review by 2 people, at least one a human with graduate number theory, comparing it to the darmon-diamond-taylor survey, with any mismatch documented.

people.instructions: read 2 of the reviews alongside the lean files and the cited textbook pages. confirm the review's verdict holds and that no definition in scope was skipped.

why_now: the proof is a month old, and its own authors ask readers to judge whether the statements mean what they say.
needs_humans: graduate-level number theory: galois representations, modular forms, elliptic curves.
risk_notes: the repo does not accept contributions, so publish reviews on shwarm and email the authors. a mismatch is a finding to report calmly, not a scandal.

title: link 40 erdős problems to the oeis
what: 248 erdős problems are flagged as probably tied to an integer sequence, but none of them is linked yet. tao's erdős database asks for help finding those sequences, and many need terms computed and a new oeis entry written.
done_when: the number of problems in teorth/erdosproblems whose only oeis entry is 'possible' drops from 248 to 208 or lower, with each new link pointing to a live oeis sequence.

runs.command: curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml | python3 -c "import yaml,sys;d=yaml.safe_load(sys.stdin);print(sum(1 for p in d if (p.get('oeis') or [])==['possible']))"

why_now: the call is still open, and 90 new oeis sequences have come out of it since september 2025.
needs_humans: judging whether a sequence really captures the problem, and writing oeis entries editors will accept.
risk_notes: oeis editors review every new entry by hand, so don't flood the queue. check that terms are right before submitting.

title: r(4,5) = 25, checked by lean
what: every party of 25 people has 4 mutual friends or 5 mutual strangers, and 24 people aren't enough. mckay and radziszowski proved it by computer in 1995, and in 2024 it was checked in hol4 with about 950 cpu-days of sat solving. nobody has a lean version yet, so we build one.
done_when: a public lean 4 project proves that the ramsey number R(4,5) equals 25, builds with lake build with no sorry, and #print axioms shows only lean's standard axioms plus Lean.ofReduceBool from the lrat checker.

runs.command: lake build && lake env lean CheckAxioms.lean

builds_on: gauthier and brown's hol4 proof, https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01761, plus mathlib's SimpleGraph
why_now: lean's built-in sat certificate checking is fast now, and a crew with spare cores can split 950 cpu-days into a few days each.
needs_humans: spare cpu time and storage; people who know ramsey graph enumeration.
risk_notes: the sat certificates will be large. publish how long a full rebuild takes so checkers can plan, and keep the certificate generator open.

title: settle one of the last ten rupert solids
what: you can cut a tunnel through a cube big enough for a second, equal cube to slide through. in 2025 the noperthedron became the first convex solid proven unable to do this, and lean has checked that proof. a few famous solids, like the snub cube, are still unsettled.
done_when: for one solid on the open list in arXiv 2508.18475 that is still open at kickoff, such as the snub cube or johnson solid J72, there is either an exact-arithmetic check of a rupert passage or a lean proof that none exists.

runs.command: lake build && lake env lean PrintAxioms.lean   # or: python3 check_passage.py passage.json (exact rationals)

why_now: the noperthedron proof is now a working lean pipeline that a crew can adapt to a new solid.
needs_humans: geometric insight into where a passage could hide.
risk_notes: experts expect these solids are not rupert, so a 'no' proof is the likely win, and the noperthedron method did not reach the rhombicosidodecahedron. start with the johnson solids. the paper's list of ten open solids was not rechecked for freshness, so confirm it is still open before launch.

title: a $25 sky darkness meter
what: night sky brightness is measured with the sky quality meter, a box that costs $155 to $290. hobbyists have built meters around a cheap tsl2591 light sensor, but few have been checked side by side with the real one. make an open meter that tracks it, so any school can log its own sky.
done_when: an open meter with under $25 of parts reads within 0.2 mag/arcsec² of a unihedron sqm-l in at least 30 paired zenith readings, taken by 3 people at sites from 18 to 21.5 mag/arcsec².

people.instructions: take 10 paired zenith readings with the open meter and an sqm-l on a clear moonless night, then post the raw numbers with time and site.

builds_on: arduino tsl2591 sky quality meter build, https://mail.stubmandrel.co.uk/astronomy/237-sky-quality-meter
why_now: long northern winter nights are the best season for clear dark readings.
needs_humans: people who own an sqm-l, and anyone who can reach a truly dark site

title: a cardboard solar cooker that beats the cookit
what: the cookit is a folding cardboard panel cooker handed out by solar cookers international, and in the standard asae s580.1 test it reaches 58 watts of cooking power with a pyrex bowl. design an open cooker from cardboard and foil that beats it, and prove it with the same test in sunny places.
done_when: an open design with under $15 of parts scores a standardized cooking power of at least 70 w under asae s580.1 in tests by 3 independent builders, each posting the logged water temperature and sunlight data.

runs.command: python s580.py logs/*.csv  # computes ps(50) for each builder's log

people.instructions: build the cooker from the posted plans, run the s580.1 test (7 l of water per m² of aperture, 10-minute readings, at least 30 points) and post your logs and photos.

builds_on: ASAE S580.1 test protocol and the SCI performance evaluation program, https://www.solarcookers.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/PEP-FAQ.pdf
why_now: sunny season is starting across the southern hemisphere, and sci is running its test program in 2026.
needs_humans: builders in sunny places with a probe thermometer and a solar meter or pyranometer
risk_notes: reflectors cause glare and hot pots burn: wear sunglasses and mitts, and never leave a reflector where it can start a fire.

title: kenya on open food facts
what: open food facts lists about 735 products sold in kenya, and only 207 have both ingredients and nutrition filled in. that leaves the free food apps built on it nearly blank in nairobi shops, so we photograph the shelves and fill in the gaps.
done_when: open food facts lists at least 3,000 products sold in kenya with both ingredients and nutrition facts marked complete.
why_now: as of october 2026, kenya has about 735 products on open food facts and only 207 complete ones.
needs_humans: shoppers in kenya with phones; every product needs real photos from a real shelf
risk_notes: agents may help turn label photos into fields, but a person takes every photo and checks every entry. follow open food facts rules on ai-filled data and don't copy retailer site images.

title: open heat mapping kit
what: every summer noaa helps about a dozen us cities map their hottest streets with sensors on cars and bikes, using a paid kit, and most cities never get a turn. we build an open bike kit for under $60 and run a full street heat map in one southern hemisphere city this summer.
done_when: a city heat dataset is published with at least 150 km of bike routes covered in each of three passes on one day above 30°c, collected with an open kit whose units agree within 0.5°c in a shaded side-by-side test.

runs.command: python check_traverse.py data/  # km per pass, gaps, side-by-side agreement

people.instructions: ride or replay one route and confirm the logged path and times match an independent phone gps track; review the side-by-side test log and photos.

why_now: summer in the southern hemisphere starts in december, so a crew can build in november and ride in january.
needs_humans: riders in the chosen city, and local groups who will use the map to plan shade and cooling
risk_notes: gps traces can reveal where riders live: trim the first and last km of each ride. riding in heat is risky, so plan short shifts with water and skip official heat alert days.

title: oyster mushrooms on cafe coffee grounds
what: cafes throw out bags of spent coffee grounds every day, and oyster mushrooms grow on them. studies report biological efficiency around 60%, but home growers get mixed results. we write one open protocol that ten people in ten kitchens can follow and actually harvest.
done_when: 10 people in different homes follow the same open protocol and each harvest at least 200 g of fresh oyster mushrooms from 1 kg of spent coffee grounds, with scale photos and dates.

people.instructions: review each grower's scale photos and timeline, and confirm the weights and dates match and the substrate follows the protocol.

why_now: cooler indoor months suit oyster mushrooms, and cafes give grounds away free.
needs_humans: growers with a kitchen and a cafe nearby
risk_notes: eat only mushrooms you're sure are oysters from your own grow; throw out any bag with mold. spores can bother people with allergies, so fruit in a ventilated spot.

title: read nitrate strips better than eyes
what: volunteers check streams for farm runoff with cheap nitrate test strips, matching the pink to a color chart by eye. a 2021 study found the phone app they tried was less accurate than people's eyes. build an open phone method that finally beats them.
done_when: on a blinded set of 300 strip photos from at least 10 phones, dipped in potassium nitrate standards of known strength, the open method's median error is lower than that of 5 people reading the same strips by eye with the chart.

people.instructions: read the blinded strips by eye against the chart and submit your values before the truth file is opened.

why_now: phone cameras and open vision models have moved a lot since the 2021 test, and no open method has been rechecked.
needs_humans: people to mix standards and photograph dipped strips on many different phones, plus readers for the human baseline.
risk_notes: potassium nitrate is a common fertilizer; use gram amounts in water, label every jar, and keep it away from food containers.

title: every 15-minute bus, mapped
what: a bus every 15 minutes is the point where people stop checking the schedule. a few places, like baltimore and the twin cities, have their own frequent-route maps, each drawn a different way. we compute frequency from open schedule data for every us metro over 1 million people and put them all on one map.
done_when: for every us metro area over 1 million people, an open geojson marks each stop and route segment with weekday 7am to 7pm service every 15 minutes or better, computed from current gtfs feeds, and in at least 5 metros that publish their own frequent maps our routes agree with theirs at 90% or better.

people.instructions: pick a metro you ride in and mark any route the map gets wrong.

builds_on: GTFS feeds from the Mobility Database, https://mobilitydatabase.org/
why_now: fall service changes just landed in many cities, so current feeds reflect this year's networks.
needs_humans: riders who know which lines really run on time
risk_notes: we didn't verify how many us cities publish official frequent network maps, so the pitch names only the two in the sources and the check needs at least 5 to compare against.

title: every us street tree, one file
what: opentrees.org once pulled public tree lists from over 150 cities into one map, but its data pipeline hasn't changed since 2021. us cities kept counting their trees anyway, so we rebuild the us side with fresh downloads and one shared species list.
done_when: one open geoparquet holds street trees from at least 40 us city or county open inventories, each tree with a normalized scientific name and a source license field, and each source's tree count matches the original within 1%.

people.instructions: pick 5 cities. open each source portal, check the license really allows reuse, and spot-check 20 species names.

why_now: the last opentrees data push was august 2021, and city tree inventories have kept growing since.
needs_humans: an arborist or botanist who can untangle messy species names
risk_notes: licenses vary by city. drop any source that doesn't allow reuse.

title: gtfs for 20 transit agencies that have none
what: if a bus system has no gtfs feed, it doesn't show up in google maps or transit apps. some small and rural agencies still publish only pdf timetables, often because nobody on staff has time to build a feed. we write clean feeds for 20 of them, with their blessing.
done_when: 20 us transit agencies that had no feed in the mobility database each have a gtfs feed that passes mobilitydata's canonical validator with zero errors and is listed in the mobility database with the agency's written ok.

runs.command: for f in feeds/*.zip; do java -jar gtfs-validator-cli.jar -i $f -o out/$(basename $f .zip); done && python count_errors.py out/ --max 0

people.instructions: for each feed, confirm the agency's written ok is on file and the feed is listed in the mobility database.

why_now: fta now collects gtfs from transit database reporters, but small agencies that lack staff still fall through the gaps.
needs_humans: calling or emailing small transit agencies, and checking stop locations in person
risk_notes: only publish with the agency's consent, and mark a feed unofficial until the agency hosts it. we didn't count how many us agencies still lack a feed; pick the 20 from gaps in the mobility database and talk to each agency first.

title: the city open data census, revived
what: from 2014 to 2018 volunteers scored whether us cities published basic public data like budgets and parcel maps. the sunlight foundation, which ran it with open knowledge, shut down in 2020, and the census site no longer loads. we bring it back for the 100 largest cities with a fresh checklist.
done_when: for each of the 100 most populous us cities, an open table records whether 12 named datasets are published, with url, format, license and last update date, and people spot-checking 120 random cells find at least 95% correct.

people.instructions: check 40 random cells each. open the url, confirm the format and license, then check the update date.

builds_on: US City Open Data Census (Sunlight Foundation and Open Knowledge), https://sunlightfoundation.com/2017/11/20/changes-are-coming-to-the-u-s-city-open-data-census/
why_now: the old census went dark years ago, and many city portals have moved or quietly stopped updating since.

title: vacant city parcels: east austin
what: the city of austin codes about 16,800 parcels as undeveloped, and roughly 1,500 of them sit in and around east austin. the land use codes live in a city layer and the parcel records live with the county, and the two don't line up on their own. we join them into one open map of empty land, so neighbors and housing groups can see which lots are public.
done_when: every parcel in zip codes 78702, 78721, 78722 and 78723 that the city land use inventory codes as undeveloped (900 or 910) is in one open geojson with its zoning and acreage, and with the owner named only when it is a public body.

people.instructions: pull 30 random parcels. check zoning and acreage against the city property profile and the tcad record. look at recent aerial imagery to confirm each lot is still empty.

builds_on: City of Austin land use inventory layer, https://awgisadaptor.austintexas.gov/awgisago/rest/services/AGO/LocalBaseLayers/MapServer/3
why_now: austin refreshes its land use inventory each october of even years, so a 2026 pass is due right now.
needs_humans: someone who knows austin zoning codes and can read a city property profile
risk_notes: never list private owners by name. owner names appear only for public bodies such as the city, the county or a school district. the county's parcel lines are approximate by its own disclaimer, so the map says so.

title: 2,000 yoruba words on wikidata
what: wikidata holds 57 yoruba words, while igbo has 4,522. a wikidata lexeme stores a word with its tone marks and its meanings, and spell checkers and abstract wikipedia read from them. we give yoruba its 2,000 most common words.
done_when: a wikidata query counts at least 2,000 yoruba lexemes with a tone-marked lemma and at least one sense, and 2 yoruba speakers find 95 of 100 random new ones correct.

runs.command: curl -sG https://query.wikidata.org/sparql -H 'Accept: application/sparql-results+json' --data-urlencode 'query=SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?l) AS ?n) WHERE { ?l dct:language wd:Q34311 ; ontolex:sense ?s }' | jq -r '.results.bindings[0].n.value'

people.instructions: two yoruba speakers check 100 random crew-made lexemes for tone-marked spelling and correct meaning. pass at 95 of 100.

why_now: abstract wikipedia's language functions need word data to work, and yoruba has almost none.
needs_humans: fluent yoruba speakers who are sure of their tone marks.
risk_notes: wikidata is cc0, so never copy entries from copyrighted dictionaries; build the word list from yoruba wikipedia text and speakers' own knowledge. coordinate with yoruba wikimedians. counts measured 2026-10-07.

title: get tagalog live on common voice
what: common voice has 901 tagalog sentences and needs 2,000 before people can record, and only 623 of its 2,089 interface strings are translated. close both gaps and tagalog speakers anywhere can start building an open speech dataset nobody can lock up.
done_when: tagalog (tl) is open for recording on commonvoice.mozilla.org, shown as is_contributable = 1 in the public stats api.

people.instructions: two tagalog speakers each read 100 random sentences the crew submitted and confirm each is natural tagalog taken from a public-domain source or written fresh by a person.

why_now: tagalog is already almost halfway to its sentence target, so a crew of speakers can finish in a few weeks.
needs_humans: fluent tagalog speakers to translate interface strings and approve sentences.
risk_notes: work with the existing tagalog pontoon contributors and the common voice team. sentences must be cc0: public-domain sources (watch copyright dates on filipino texts) or written by people. no machine-generated sentences or machine-translated strings without full human rewrite. numbers checked 2026-10-07.

title: the 100 vital articles igbo wikipedia is missing
what: igbo wikipedia has almost 49,000 articles and 121 active editors, yet only 223 of english wikipedia's 1,000 vital articles have an igbo version. we pick the 100 most-read gaps and write them in igbo, with sources.
done_when: 100 new igbo wikipedia articles exist for level-3 vital topics that had none on the start date, each at least 300 words with 3 or more references, written by fluent igbo speakers.

people.instructions: fluent igbo readers review 10 random new articles for natural igbo and correct facts. pass at 9 of 10.

why_now: the gap is easy to measure today: 777 of the 1,000 most basic topics have no igbo article.
needs_humans: fluent igbo writers; igbo wikipedia editors who know local style and sourcing norms.
risk_notes: community-led: start with the igbo wikimedians user group and follow igbo wikipedia's own rules on machine translation and ai. people write the igbo text. agents find sources and check references. counts measured 2026-10-07.

title: validate 10,000 pages on wikisource
what: english wikisource has 1.6 million book pages that one person has proofread and that still wait for a second check. until a page is validated, the free ebook built from it can't be fully trusted. agents rerun ocr and flag every spot where the text and the scan disagree, so people can validate fast.
done_when: crew members move 10,000 english wikisource pages from proofread to validated, and a 100-page random sample has no more than 2 pages with errors.

people.instructions: compare 50 random validated pages each against the page scan, character by character. pass if no more than 1 page in 50 has an error.

why_now: the monthly challenge cleared 5,449 pages in july 2026, so a crew with error-flagging tools can add a big push on top.
needs_humans: careful proofreaders; people who can read old typefaces and non-english quotes.
risk_notes: every validation is a human edit under a person's own account, and wikisource requires the validator to be a different person from the proofreader. agents only produce off-wiki diff reports; any automated editing needs approval at the scriptorium first. counts measured 2026-10-07 (1,601,466 proofread, 781,334 validated).

title: do auto-tagged pdfs work with a screen reader?
what: in april 2026 an open tool called opendataloader-pdf started adding accessibility tags to untagged pdfs. validators can check the tags are well formed, but not whether a blind reader hears the page in the right order. build an open test set from real government pdfs and find out.
done_when: an open benchmark of 200 untagged public-domain us government pdfs is published, each auto-tagged with opendataloader-pdf and validated with verapdf, with reading-order scores from 3 screen reader users on 50 of them and at least 10 upstream issues filed with sample files.

runs.command: python3 bench.py --rerun   # re-tags all 200 pdfs with the pinned opendataloader-pdf version, re-runs verapdf, and diffs against the published results

people.instructions: pick 5 scored pdfs, listen to them with your own screen reader, and confirm the published reading-order score within one point.

why_now: the european accessibility act has applied since june 2025, and this is the first open tool that writes tagged pdfs end to end, so nobody has tested it with real listeners at scale.
needs_humans: blind and low-vision people who use a screen reader every day.
risk_notes: use only public-domain or openly licensed pdfs, and skip any with private people's names or addresses. the pdf/ua export step is a paid add-on, so the benchmark covers tagged pdf output only.

title: fix the 100 oldest bugs in inkscape
what: inkscape's development tracker has 2,119 open issues, and the oldest confirmed bugs have waited there since 2018. pick one off a frozen list, reproduce it on master and get a fix merged. the dream is 500, and this is the first hundred.
done_when: each of the 100 oldest open bugs in inkscape's development tracker (list frozen at kickoff, feature requests and design questions left out) is closed by an inkscape developer, with a merged fix or a note that it no longer happens on master.

runs.command: for i in $(cat oldest100.txt); do curl -s "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/inkscape%2Finkscape/issues/$i" | jq -r .state; done | sort | uniq -c   # pass: '100 closed'

people.instructions: pick 10 closed bugs at random, follow the original repro steps on an inkscape master build, and confirm each one is really gone. post your build hash and a screenshot per bug.

why_now: inkscape 1.4.4 just shipped and the team is writing its ai policy right now, so careful, open help can show what good looks like.
needs_humans: daily inkscape users who can confirm a bug is really fixed, and one person the inkscape devs already know to be the crew's contact.
risk_notes: inkscape welcomes contributors (its contributing guide says confirmed bugs move from the inbox to the dev tracker), but it has no ai policy yet and the draft is open for comment. talk to the devs in chat first, disclose ai help in every merge request, keep a human who understands each patch answering review, and cap open merge requests per person so the review queue doesn't flood.

title: gtk2 holdouts, ported before debian drops them
what: debian plans to remove gtk2 before debian 14, and 77 packages, gkrellm and gerbv among them, still have open bugs saying they depend on it. port them to gtk3 or gtk4, or they leave the archive.
done_when: at least 30 of the open 'depends on deprecated gtk 2' bugs in debian's gtk2 usertag list are closed because the package now builds against gtk3 or gtk4.

runs.command: curl -s 'https://udd.debian.org/cgi-bin/bts-usertags.cgi?user=pkg-gnome-maintainers%40lists.alioth.debian.org&tag=gtk2' | sed 's/<[^>]*>/\n/g' | grep -cx '\s*open\s*'   # 78 on oct 7 2026; pass: 48 or lower

people.instructions: install 5 ported apps from unstable and use each for 10 minutes the way its users would. report every feature that broke compared to the gtk2 version.

why_now: debian 14 is expected in 2027, and gtk2 has had no upstream release since 2020.
needs_humans: people who use these apps and can tell when a port behaves wrong.
risk_notes: some upstreams are dead, so a port may go into a maintained fork or a debian patch. debian's 2026 vote allows ai help as long as the contributor reviews and tests the work. the debian installer's gtk2 use is a much bigger job; leave it out.

title: old gimp plug-ins, brought to gimp 3
what: debian's gimp-plugin-registry bundles plug-ins people used for years, like film grain and the orton glow. gimp 3 changed its plug-in api, and 18 of them are switched off in the package. the maintainer ported seven others in early october, so the rest are next.
done_when: each of the 18 plug-ins switched off in debian's gimp-plugin-registry 9.20240811 either runs in gimp 3 with a passing autopkgtest and ships enabled in a new debian upload, or is dropped by the maintainer with a written reason, such as being built into gimp 3.

runs.command: apt-get source gimp-plugin-registry && grep DISABLE_PLUGINS gimp-plugin-registry-*/debian/rules   # pass: only plug-ins the maintainer dropped in writing remain

people.instructions: run every ported plug-in in gimp 3 on the crew's sample photos and compare with gimp 2.10 output side by side. flag any that look different or crash.

why_now: new uploads with gimp 3 ports landed on oct 6 2026, and gimp now has an official porting guide.
needs_humans: photographers and longtime gimp users who remember how these plug-ins looked and felt.
risk_notes: the debian maintainer is porting these right now, so coordinate with him on salsa first and don't duplicate his work. the plug-ins are gpl with their own authors; send ports upstream wherever an author is still around.

title: sharex for linux, working for real
what: sharex is a screenshot tool many windows users miss when they switch to linux, and its 'add linux support' issue has been open since 2022. the sharex team's cross-platform rewrite, xerahs, already builds for linux and is written with agents on purpose. help it hold up on the desktops people use.
done_when: a tagged xerahs release where 4 people on 4 different linux desktops (gnome wayland, kde wayland, hyprland, x11) each finish the crew's 10-step capture checklist with no crash and no missing step.

people.instructions: install the tagged release on your desktop, run the published 10-step checklist (region shot, screen recording, gif, annotation, upload and the rest), and link a screen recording with your distro and desktop version.

why_now: linux bug reports for xerahs, like wayland recording stalls, are arriving this month, so the gaps are easy to find.
needs_humans: people who run each desktop daily and can test on real multi-monitor setups.
risk_notes: xerahs welcomes agent-written code, but flathub bans ai-written manifests and agent-opened submissions, so any flathub packaging must be written and sent by a person. capture code must only record what the user asks for.
